stories.title: Frankfurt twin blasts: Dutch 17-year-old arrested; no injuries

facts.text: Early Thu (~04:00): explosions minutes apart damaged a café in Frankfurt-Nordend and a kiosk on Zeil; no injuries reported (DW; Anadolu).
Police: 17-year-old Dutch national arrested near the Nordend scene; due before a judge (Anadolu / police statement).
Café blast also damaged a soup bar across the street, an adjacent bank, and at least one parked car; residents described a war-like bang (Anadolu; Hessenschau via AA).

Context: further Rhine-Main blasts in recent days (Frankfurt + Offenbach), prior Sachsenhausen arrest of a 15-year-old; police have linked some regional cases to organized “violence as a service” recruiting teens (DW).

stories.whyItMatters: Another overnight blast cluster in Germany’s financial hub — with a quick arrest — keeps the Rhine-Main bombing wave on the front page ahead of Sunday’s state votes.

stories.title: US stocks bounce after Fed sell-off; 10-year back under 5%

facts.text: Thu session (Yahoo ~19:30 Berlin): S&P 500 ~7632 (+~1.1% vs Wed close), Nasdaq ~26386 (+~1.6%), Dow ~51789 (+~0.6%).
CNBC / NBC morning tape: Dow was up ~300–450 pts early as yields and oil softened after Wed’s first Fed hike since 2023 (Warsh).
10-year Treasury yield ~4.955% (Yahoo) after touching ~5.02% Wed; NBC noted a dip toward ~4.96% with the bond rally.
Oil: WTI ~$102.2 (−0.2% session), Brent ~$104.7 (−1.1%); NBC said WTI briefly slipped under $100 overnight before rebounding (not confirmed at this print).
Street caution: Citadel’s Rubner and JPMorgan desks still tactically cautious into month-end / September seasonality despite the bounce (CNBC).

stories.whyItMatters: Markets are treating Warsh’s hike as a credibility reset — but desks still warn the relief rally can fade if oil/yields re-spike.

stories.title: Ukraine: ≥10 killed, 75 injured in past-day Russian strikes

facts.text: Kyiv Independent (updated Thu afternoon): ≥10 killed and 75 injured across Ukraine over the past day; main overnight targets Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa oblasts.
Air Force: of 157 drones + 10 “Banderol” cruise missiles in the wave from Wed evening, 124 drones and 7 Banderols shot down/suppressed; hits at 36 locations (Kyiv Independent).
Kyiv: Mayor Klitschko said 20 people injured including two children (revised upward from morning tallies).
Morning brief already covered the overnight wave and the House Graham sanctions bill — this is the fuller past-day casualty update, not a new sanction story.

stories.whyItMatters: Casualty figures climbed through the day after morning’s early injure counts — the overnight barrage was larger than the first DW/AFP snippets suggested.

stories.title: Klingbeil + auto-state premiers push EU tariffs on Chinese hybrids

facts.text: At VW Wolfsburg Thu, Vice Chancellor/Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil urged the EU to widen China tariffs to plug-in hybrids and tighten local-content rules (DW).
Coordinated letter from Bavaria (Söder), Baden-Württemberg (Özdemir) and Lower Saxony (Lies) premiers: without protective instruments + fair WTO trade, irreversible damage to the auto industry (DW).
Afternoon brief already had the FT angle on Brussels seeking voluntary Chinese hybrid-export curbs (~15% EU share) — this is Berlin/Länder escalating toward tariff parity with BEVs.
Context DW: VW’s approved restructuring can phase out up to ~100k jobs; German auto shed >50k jobs in 2025 alone.

stories.whyItMatters: German coalition economics and the three carmaking states are now openly lobbying Brussels for hybrid tariffs — a step beyond this afternoon’s voluntary-curb ask.
